A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are seeking for a deeper understanding of the users’ response when interacting with a new technology that is based on semantic web technologies.

the users’ response and acceptance of the ontology based systems is a result of a complex socio-cognitive process that is affected by several factors, including: the users’ prior knowledge about the ontology based systems, the users’ knowledge and beliefs about the enterprise, and the users’ knowledge about the enterprise’s goals and objectives.
ontology based technologies can provide an efficient and flexible approach in supporting the users’ knowledge acquisition and learning process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
users are not necessarily ready to accept the new knowledge paradigm brought by the semantic web.
the users’ response towards ontology-based systems is not a simple matter of acceptance/rejection, but it is more a process that evolves through the users’ interaction with the system.

the use of ontology based systems in a virtual community context can be seen as a learning process, which is based on the individual’s cognitive and social abilities to acquire and assimilate the new technology and its underlying concepts.
